t19: The large group game problem can be summed up in one sentence: people waiting for their turn get bored. In a group larger than 8, games played with the traditional "now it's your turn" logic fall apart. The solution is not to change the game but to change the game's structure.
t21: You can't form teams with two people, so the "describe–guess" logic works directly head-to-head. Your opponent is also the guesser; the score is kept accordingly.
t23: Modes where everyone plays at the same time
t25: — A question is read, everyone points with their finger at the same time. No waiting, no turns.
t27: — A statement is read, everyone says "true" or "false." Sixteen people play in a single round.
t29: — A letter is given, everyone fills their own list at the same time. When time is up, common count is done.
t31: Choosing teams manually takes five minutes and usually the same three people stay together. Random division is both fairer and faster.
t32: Use a random team selector: enter names, let the app divide evenly.
t33: Adjust team count by player count: 2 teams for 8 people, 3 for 12, 4 for 16.
t34: Change the storyteller within the team each round; when the same person keeps telling, others become spectators.
t35: Modes played simultaneously completely eliminate the waiting-in-line problem for large groups.
t36: Adjusting round time for large groups
t37: Total time in large groups grows quickly. In a group of 12 with 90-second rounds, a single round lasts 18 minutes. Reducing round time to 45–60 seconds brings that same round down to 10 minutes and transitions to the next round without losing momentum.
t38: Practical measure: total game time should not exceed 25 minutes. Once it does, taking a break and switching to a different mode gives better results than forcing the same game longer.
t39: Bringing a bored person back into the game
t40: Give spectators a "jury" role: let them make the right/wrong decision.
t41: Count the score out loud; people tend to return as the score is heard.
t42: Play one round entirely with a mode chosen by a completely new player.

t46: Which game do you play with 10 people?
t47: With groups of ten, team-based word games (Tabu, Sessiz Kelime) and poll-based modes played simultaneously give the best results. Avoid long turn-based games.
